subject: Mathematics
title: Sets, Relations and Functions
summary: Set ek well-defined collection hai. Operations — union, intersection, difference, complement — De Morgan's laws follow karte hain, aur inclusion–exclusion principle union ke elements ginta hai. Saare subsets ka set power set hai.
A se B tak relation A × B ka koi bhi subset hai. Set par relation reflexive, symmetric, transitive ho sakta hai (teeno = equivalence relation, jo set ko equivalence classes mein baant deta hai).

Function domain ke har element ko theek ek image deta hai. Functions one-one (injective), onto (surjective) ya dono (bijective) ho sakte hain; sirf bijections ka inverse hota hai. Composition fog se functions jodte hain.
JEE ko counting questions bahut pasand hain: relations, functions, one-one aur onto maps, aur reflexive ya symmetric relations ki ginti.

formulas.name: Inclusion–exclusion (2 sets)
formulas.formula: n(A ∪ B) = n(A) + n(B) − n(A ∩ B)

formulas.name: Inclusion–exclusion (3 sets)
formulas.formula: n(A ∪ B ∪ C) = Σn(A) − Σn(A ∩ B) + n(A ∩ B ∩ C)

formulas.name: Power set
formulas.formula: n(P(A)) = 2ⁿ for n(A) = n;  proper subsets = 2ⁿ − 1

formulas.name: Cartesian product and relations
formulas.formula: n(A × B) = mn;  number of relations from A to B = 2^{mn}

formulas.name: Relations on a set with n elements
formulas.formula: total 2^{n²};  reflexive 2^{n² − n};  symmetric 2^{n(n+1)/2};  reflexive and symmetric 2^{n(n−1)/2}

formulas.name: Equivalence relation
formulas.formula: reflexive (a R a) + symmetric (a R b ⇒ b R a) + transitive (a R b, b R c ⇒ a R c)
formulas.mistake: Non-empty set par empty relation symmetric aur transitive hai par reflexive nahi — dhyan rakho.

formulas.name: Counting functions (m-set → n-set)
formulas.formula: all functions nᵐ;  one-one nPm (m ≤ n);  onto Σ (−1)ᵏ C(n, k)(n − k)ᵐ (m ≥ n);  bijections n! (m = n)

formulas.name: Even and odd functions
formulas.formula: even f(−x) = f(x) (symmetric about y-axis);  odd f(−x) = −f(x) (symmetric about origin);  every f = even part + odd part

formulas.name: Composition and inverse
formulas.formula: (g∘f)(x) = g(f(x));  (g∘f)⁻¹ = f⁻¹∘g⁻¹;  f⁻¹ exists ⇔ f bijective;  graphs of f and f⁻¹ are mirror images in y = x

formulas.name: Greatest integer and fractional part
formulas.formula: [x] ≤ x < [x] + 1;  {x} = x − [x] ∈ [0, 1);  [x + n] = [x] + n for integer n

formulas.name: Periodic functions
formulas.formula: period of sin, cos = 2π;  tan, cot = π;  {x} = 1;  |sin x| = π;  period of f(ax + b) = T/|a|

topics.title: Types of sets
topics.explain: Empty (∅), singleton, finite, infinite, equal sets, equivalent sets (same cardinality), subsets, universal set. Intervals: open (a, b), closed [a, b], half-open.

topics.title: Symmetric difference
topics.explain: A Δ B = (A − B) ∪ (B − A) = (A ∪ B) − (A ∩ B). Venn-diagram wale sawalon mein kaam aata hai.

topics.title: Equivalence classes
topics.explain: A par equivalence relation A ko disjoint classes mein baant deta hai. Example: integers par R = {(a, b): a − b, 3 se divisible} ki teen classes — remainders 0, 1, 2.

topics.title: Checking one-one and onto
topics.explain: One-one: f(x₁) = f(x₂) ⇒ x₁ = x₂, ya f strictly monotonic; horizontal line test. Onto: range = codomain. Finite set se usi set tak function one-one tabhi hai jab onto ho.

topics.title: Range-finding techniques
topics.explain: y = f(x) likh kar x ke liye solve karo, phir y par conditions nikalo; monotonicity, completing the square ya AM–GM inequality use karo; x² wale rational functions ke liye discriminant ≥ 0.

topics.title: Special functions
topics.explain: Modulus |x|, signum sgn x (1, 0, −1), greatest integer [x], fractional part {x}, exponential aur logarithmic functions. Inke graphs, domains aur ranges yaad rakho.
